explanation: BigQuery charges for the data a query reads, not for the rows it sends back. The suffix filter keeps the narrow query to the October daily tables. The wide one has no suffix filter, so events_* reads every daily table, and its WHERE on event_date only drops rows after they are read: a filter on event_date does not choose which daily tables are read. A LIMIT would not change the data read either, on tables that are not clustered.
